methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses multiple complementary model systems (established prostate cancer lines, patient-derived CRPC organoids, and an in vivo NSG xenograft/PDX subline) to test vulnerability of an AR-negative/WNT-dependent subtype to SMARCA2/4 degraders, which is an appropriate design for mechanistic therapeutic claims. Key quality controls are described (mycoplasma testing, STR authentication, passage limits), and the in vivo experiment specifies tumor-size criteria, dosing (A947 40 mg/kg IV), monitoring cadence, and a blinded veterinary pathology readout. The work also leverages scRNA-seq to assess transcriptomic effects of degrader versus control epimer in two CRPC-WNT organoid models with explicit QC pass counts per condition, supporting mechanistic conclusions. Limitations include limited detail on randomization/blinding for all in vivo measurements, no stated power calculation for the xenograft arm, and unclear multiplicity correction across high-dimensional transcriptomic analyses beyond standard adjusted P value procedures.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The evidence base is preclinical (cell lines, organoids, and mouse xenograft/PDX modeling) without patient-outcome testing, mapping to Oxford LoE 5. Clinically, the work targets a defined castration-resistant, AR-negative subtype and frames it as an unmet-need population, which increases translational relevance even without direct clinical endpoints. The in vivo tumor growth delay after a single degrader dose and the mechanistic linkage to a lineage-defining WNT/TCF7L2 axis provide a plausible therapeutic rationale. However, applicability to patient care remains indirect pending clinical biomarker stratification and safety/PK-PD characterization.

reporting_quality.justification: Given the central reliance on animal xenograft work, ARRIVE is the closest applicable reporting framework, and many practical animal-handling and endpoint details are explicitly described (strain/age, housing, ethics license, dosing formulation, tumor-volume formula, and maximum burden). Methods are generally granular for wet-lab assays (antibodies listed; imaging/quantification tools; compound sourcing) and for scRNA-seq processing/QC (cells passing QC per condition, normalization/clustering tools and parameters). Some ARRIVE-style elements are incomplete or not explicit in the normalized text, including formal randomization strategy, blinding for caliper measurements, and sample-size justification. The manuscript does not clearly specify public deposition of sequencing data or code in the normalized version, so reproducibility posture appears limited to methods description.

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is extending SWI/SNF ATPase degrader vulnerability beyond AR-driven CRPC into a double-negative, WNT-dependent CRPC subtype and tying this to disruption of a lineage-defining TCF7L2 regulatory axis. The paper adds mechanistic positioning by connecting TCF7L2 activity to proproliferative MAPK signaling and by using transcriptomic profiling to show mitigation of a CRPC-WNT signature with degrader treatment. SWI/SNF targeting and lineage plasticity in prostate cancer are active areas, so the conceptual space is not entirely new, but the subtype-specific dependency and degrader-based intervention are meaningful. The findings are more than incremental because they nominate a therapeutically actionable axis in a defined minority CRPC subgroup.

writing_presentation.justification: The narrative is coherent: the introduction motivates lineage plasticity and defines the CRPC-WNT subgroup, then the results move from pharmacologic degradation effects to mechanistic transcriptional regulation and in vivo validation. Methods include practical details that make the experimental workflow interpretable (drug sources, dosing, xenograft monitoring, STR/mycoplasma controls). The abstract states a clear mechanistic claim (SMARCA4 depletion affecting TCF7L2 and MAPK signaling) that aligns with the core results. As a limitation, the density of subtype nomenclature and multi-omic analyses may require careful signposting to keep causal claims distinct from correlative transcriptomic observations.

key_strengths: Subtype-focused preclinical evaluation using both CRPC-WNT organoids and an in vivo xenograft/PDX subline treated with a SMARCA2/4 degrader
Clear laboratory quality controls (mycoplasma testing, STR authentication, passage limits) and detailed compound sourcing
Mechanistic positioning linking SWI/SNF perturbation to a lineage-defining WNT/TCF7L2 program with downstream pathway implications
key_concerns: No explicit sample-size/power justification for the in vivo study and incomplete detail on randomization/blinding procedures
Data/code availability statements and public deposition of high-dimensional data are not clearly present in the normalized manuscript
Multiplicity and robustness details for transcriptomic analyses are only partially visible, which can weaken confidence in some differential-signature claims
Clinical translation remains speculative without prospective biomarker validation in patient samples beyond organoid models
chief_reviewer.rationale: The work supports a strong tier-2 mechanistic translational paper centered on a defined CRPC subtype, but it needs tighter rigor/reporting around in vivo experimental design and clearer reproducibility disclosures to meet that bar.
